categories.tree: Parse `input` and emit its canonical tree (STXT-TREE-SPEC); it must equal `expected`, compared as a JSON value, never as text.
categories.parse-error: Parsing `input` must fail; the first error reported must carry `error.code` and `error.line` (1-based).
categories.validate: `definitions` is a list of sets of definition files (schemas or templates, by their `.schema.stxt` / `.template.stxt` suffix). For every set: load its files into one provider, parse `input` and validate each of its root nodes. There must be no error, with every set (a schema and its template must behave the same).
categories.validate-error: Same, but with every set the first error reported must carry `error.code` and `error.line` (STXT-SCHEMA-SPEC §13.1).
categories.definition-error: Loading `input` as a definition of `kind` (`schema` or `template`) must fail; the first error must carry `error.code` and `error.line` (STXT-SCHEMA-SPEC §13.1, STXT-TEMPLATE-SPEC §14.1; `line` 0 when the error is about the whole document).

cases.description: A blank line of a block is "" however it is written, and a block whose only line is blank is [""], not [].
Indentation beyond the level of the block is literal content and is kept.
Inside a block, ':', '>>' and '#' are literal text.
A block node can be a root node.
A BOM and CRLF line endings are accepted; the BOM and every trailing CR are discarded.
A comment at the level of the block node (or shallower) closes the block.
A comment is validated like a node but never moves the hierarchy.
A document without nodes has an empty tree.
Combining marks (Mn, Mc) are name characters.
The logical name is trimmed and its inner whitespace runs compacted; the canonical name compacts every run of separators into one '-'.
Canonical names keep accents and are case-insensitive: 'Caña' and 'Cana' are different, 'Straße' and 'STRASSE' too (lower-casing, not case folding).
A child may redeclare the namespace; its descendants inherit the new one and later siblings keep the old one.
Blanks are only U+0020 and U+0009: a no-break space is content, neither trimmed nor making a line empty.
canonicalName is NFC; name keeps the characters as they were written.
Four spaces are one level, like a tab.
The normative example of the specification: namespace lower-cased and inherited, a block with blank lines, a second root without lateral inheritance.
Inline values are trimmed; block lines are right-trimmed only, inner blank lines are kept, and the block ends at the first non-empty line at its level.
Two spaces of indentation: spaces must be a multiple of 4.
Six spaces of indentation: not a multiple of 4 even though it is more than one level.
A tab followed by a space in the indentation of one line.
A space followed by a tab in the indentation of one line.
A jump of two levels right after a root.
A jump of two levels after a nested node.
Eight spaces after a root: a valid multiple of 4 but a jump of two levels.
The first node of the document is indented: before the first node the reference level is -1.
An indented comment before any node is a level jump too.
Content after the >> of a block node.
Content after the >> of a nested block node.
A no-break space after >> is content, not a blank.
Mixed indentation inside a block line is still an error.
Mixed indentation inside a block line, space first.
A nested line with neither ':' nor '>>'.
The '>>' precedes the ':': neither an inline node nor a clean block.
The logical name is the empty string.
A block node with an empty name.
A line holding only a no-break space is not empty: it is a line without separator.
A character that is not a letter, digit, mark, '-', '_' or space.
Only separators: the canonical name is the empty string.
A combining mark alone: a name needs at least a letter or a digit.
An enclosing mark (Me) is not a name character; only Mn and Mc are.
A no-break space is not trimmed from the name, and it is not a name character.
A no-break space inside the name.
An invalid name in a nested node reports the line of that node.
A namespace needs at least two segments.
Only [a-z0-9] per segment: '-' is not allowed.
The '@' prefix needs a namespace after it.
A comment with a tab and a space in its indentation.
A comment indented with three spaces.
A comment two levels deeper than the last node.
A comment never moves the hierarchy: the node after it is checked against the last node.
After a comment closes a block, a deeper line is a level jump, not block text.
After a comment closes a root block, every node is closed and the reference level is -1: a level-1 line is a level jump.
GROUP: a >> block is a value, and GROUP allows none.
INLINE without declared Children: any child is undeclared; the error is at the child's line.
ENUM declares no Children, so a child is CHILD_NOT_DECLARED (closed model comes first), at the child's line.
Any Node of the schema can be a root node.
Several roots of the same namespace validate independently.
The order of the children is not validated.
A child not declared in Children (closed model).
Any child under a Node without Children.
A root whose name is not a Node of the schema.
Names and namespaces match by canonical form: 'TITLE' is Title and 'note' is Note.
'Title' and 'title' are the same child: two of them exceed Max 1.
A node with no namespace is never validated.
A non-empty namespace with no definition available.
A child of another namespace is validated against that namespace's definition.
An error inside the other namespace is reported there.
The other namespace has no definition available.
The child inherits the namespace of its root.
The root is not 'Schema': the meta-schema has no such Node. The definition is validated against the meta-schema first, so the error comes from the document table of §13.1.
The root namespace is not @stxt.schema: no definition for it in the meta provider. The definition is validated against the meta-schema first, so the error comes from the document table of §13.1.
The target namespace is not valid.
No Node at all (the meta-schema requires at least one).
A Node written as a block: the meta-schema declares it INLINE. The definition is validated against the meta-schema first, so the error comes from the document table of §13.1.
Two Node with the same canonical name. The error is about the schema as a whole: line 0.
A Node whose value is not a valid name.
A Child whose value is not a valid name.
Unknown type: the meta-schema catches it as INVALID_VALUE of the Type ENUM.
Values on a type other than ENUM; reported at the line of the Node.
Min is not a NATURAL: the meta-schema catches it first.
Two Min: the meta-schema allows at most one.
A Values that holds no Value: the meta-schema requires at least one. The definition is validated against the meta-schema first, so the error comes from the document table of §13.1.
Two Values nodes: the meta-schema allows at most one.
Two Child with the same canonical name and namespace. Line 0: about the schema as a whole.
A Child of the own namespace without its Node. Line 0: about the schema as a whole.
A cross-namespace Child needs no Node; the error here is the duplicated Node (line 0).
A member the meta-schema does not declare.
The root is not 'Template': the meta-template has no such Node. The definition is validated against the meta-template first, so the error comes from the document table of STXT-SCHEMA-SPEC §13.1.
The target namespace is not valid.
No Structure: the meta-template requires it (Min 1). The definition is validated against the meta-template first, so the error comes from the document table of STXT-SCHEMA-SPEC §13.1.
Structure is not a block: the meta-template declares it BLOCK. The definition is validated against the meta-template first, so the error comes from the document table of STXT-SCHEMA-SPEC §13.1.
A Structure line with neither ':' nor '>>': the block is parsed as STXT, so it is INVALID_LINE of STXT-SPEC, at the line of the template.
A cardinality that is not a known form.
An unclosed parenthesis: the rule part of the line does not follow §6.2.
A value list on a type other than ENUM.
A local node (B, already defined under A) appears again under C without @.
A reference to a node never defined.
B is already defined, and the name after @ is not B.
A reference and an explicit type on the same line.
A reference that declares ENUM values.
A trailing comma is an empty value.
An explicit type on a cross-namespace node.
A value list on a cross-namespace node.
A Description entry with no node in Structure.
A Description entry with another namespace.
Two Description entries for the same node.
The content of Description does not parse as STXT.
D is not defined yet, so '@B' on its line is a reference that resolves to nothing (not a name mismatch).
